title: IC-Link and TSMC expand access to advanced chip design
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Through TSMC's OIP Cloud Alliance, the collaboration combines secure cloud-based design capabilities with access to advanced node technology and expert support to help innovators bring chips to market faster.

IC-Link by imec and TSMC announced on September 23, 2026, that they are expanding their collaboration to help customers design chips using TSMC’s advanced manufacturing processes. IC-Link is joining TSMC’s Open Innovation Platform Cloud Alliance and says it will offer the alliance’s first managed cloud service that supports design flows using tools from multiple electronic design automation partners.

The service brings several resources together: controlled access to TSMC process design kits, scalable computing capacity, secure hosting, infrastructure management and IC-Link’s design support. Customers can use their preferred design tools and existing licenses. That flexibility matters because developing an advanced chip requires more than choosing a manufacturing process; teams also need substantial computing power, compatible tools and a secure way to work with sensitive design information.

Why it matters: For a startup, research group or smaller chip company, assembling that infrastructure can consume time and engineering effort before a design is ready for manufacture. A managed environment could make it easier to start work on advanced designs and shorten the path from an idea to a finished chip. IC-Link and TSMC identify artificial intelligence, communications, automotive and industrial applications among the potential uses.

The announcement also extends an established relationship. IC-Link has participated in TSMC’s Design Center Alliance since 2007 and Value Chain Alliance since 2009, and joined its 3DFabric Alliance earlier in 2026. The new cloud offering adds design infrastructure to that broader set of services.

The practical test will be whether customers can use the service to complete designs faster and bring them to market. The announcement sets out that goal, but does not report customer results or quantify a reduction in development time.
